sampling_model.design: Uniformly draw an ordered tuple of \(G_n\) pairwise-disjoint \(M\)-subsets of \(\mathcal U_n\), then independently and completely randomize exactly \(G_{1n}\) group labels to treatment.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) labeled units and every composition-indexed potential outcome are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is shared within each realized group, with \(p_n=G_{1n}/G_n\to p\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The grouped-unit fraction satisfies \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\); no birthday-scale condition on \(N_n^2/n\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The latent object affecting exact variance is \(E_{\tau,1,n}\), the degree-one Johnson energy of the arm difference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency for a fixed finite menu of admissible group sizes under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\).
Theorem 3 and the Johnson-scheme discussion provide an orthogonal harmonic basis and common eigenspaces for functions on a slice.
Proposition 3.1 records the classical eigenvalues for distance graphs in the Johnson scheme, including the Kneser relation.
Theorems 3--4 establish finite-population Gaussian limits for complete randomization on fixed experimental units.
Theorem 1 makes CR2 exactly unbiased under a specified independent-cluster working covariance model.
Theorem 1 relates regression sandwich estimators to conservative Neyman variances when clusters are fixed.
The paper characterizes optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs because exact variance is generally unavailable.
Theorems 1--2 show that design-unbiased estimators can fail to concentrate under arbitrary or network interference.

body.tldr: Randomly formed groups cease to behave as independent regression clusters when a positive fraction of eligible units is partitioned. The normalized Kneser operator gives an unconditional exact variance identity and a schedule-uniform expansion in which only the degree-one Johnson projection of the arm difference survives at first order. The ambient class \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) contains the growth, fraction, boundedness, and scaled-variance conditions, but not predictable quadratic-variation stabilization. The centered Gaussian theorem is instead an implication for each array in that class satisfying the additional filtration-side premise \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\); CR2 studentization and coverage are conditional on the same premise, whereas the variance and CR2 expansions and their ratio comparisons are unconditional. At positive density CR2 is conservative and is ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible. At zero density it yields studentized normality without \(N_n^2/n\to0\), conditional on the explicit premise. The eight-unit witness has exact variance \(1/7\) and expected CR2 \(2/7\). No one-realization estimator is uniformly ratio-consistent for exact variance even on the additive no-interference subclass; the Rademacher supports used for that lower bound separately satisfy predictable-variation stability, so the lower bound transfers upward to the enlarged arbitrary-composition class.

project_justification.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} defines PAME and validates clustered inference by coupling the whole disjoint group tuple to independent draws under its Assumption 1 and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). That approximation discards first-order finite-pool dependence when \(N_n/n\to\rho>0\), while fixed-cluster CR2 does not restore it. Bounded composition schedules also do not by themselves establish predictable quadratic-variation stabilization for the exact reveal filtration.
project_justification.niche: The disjointness relation is a Kneser operator on the uniform \(M\)-slice, so exact causal variance and the CR2 comparison can be decomposed unconditionally by Johnson degree before a Gaussian approximation is invoked. The ambient schedule class is kept separate from the statistic-specific filtration premise, which appears only as an antecedent of the CLT, studentization, and coverage conclusions.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact spectrum-weighted variance, the schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) dense expansion, and the unconditional CR2 fluctuation bound; proves that only degree one survives at the \(G_n\)-scale; and proves centered martingale normality and Wald coverage whenever an array in the ambient class additionally satisfies \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\). It also characterizes the unconditional CR2 sharpness frontier, verifies the versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) consumer and the finite witness, and proves an all-statistic exact-variance impossibility theorem using a construction-specific predictable-variation calculation and deterministic diagonal selection.

body.related_work: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} is the closest theorem-level comparator: its Section 3 permits a fixed finite menu of group sizes, and its Theorems 1--2 obtain asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). The present positive theory treats the exact homogeneous \(K=1\) structural subcase. Its exact Kneser variance and CR2 expansions are unconditional under the stated fixed-size design conditions, whereas its Gaussian and coverage conclusions replace the comparator's inference conditions by scaled-variance nondegeneracy and the explicit statistic-specific antecedent \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\). This is an assumption trade, not a pure weakening, because predictable-variation stabilization is not derived for every bounded schedule and is not included in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\). Positive homogeneous conclusions are not claimed for variable group sizes. Theorems 1 and 3 and the Johnson association-scheme discussion of \cite{Filmus2016} provide the harmonic architecture; Proposition 3.1 of \cite{BrouwerEtAl2018} supplies the classical Kneser spectrum, and the present work derives the causal covariance quadratic form. Section 2.2 and Theorems 3--4 of \cite{LiDing2017} inform complete randomization, while \cite{Pollard1984}, Theorem VIII.1, supplies the martingale-array implication once predictable variation and conditional Lindeberg are available. The versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) 0.7.0 and \({\tt sandwich}\) 3.1-3 source contracts supply the software assembly, default-target, adjustment, bread, and scale semantics used by the exact consumer proposition; \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} explains CR2 calibration under independent-cluster working models, and \cite{SuDing2021} gives the fixed-cluster design-based regression comparison. None supplies the random-partition projection correction. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} studies optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds when exact variance is inaccessible, and \cite{BasseAiroldi2018} supplies general interference nonconcentration logic; neither subsumes the equal-observation dense-PAME lower bound proved here. That lower bound holds on an additive no-interference subclass whose supports separately satisfy predictable-variation stability, and therefore transfers to the enlarged arbitrary-composition class. \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} gives sharp variance bounds for ordinary complete randomization, whereas global composition-table completion is a distinct unselected seed. \cite{BasseDingFellerToulis2024} and \cite{PuelzBasseFellerToulis2022} obtain exact tests by making peer-effect nulls sharp through symmetry or conditioning; PAME remains non-sharp from one random partition.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Finite-sample CR2 conservativeness is not asserted: the exact bias is \(-C_{\tau\tau,n}\), and higher Johnson eigenvalues alternate in sign. Conservativeness emerges at the \(G_n\)-scale because only the negative degree-one eigenvalue survives. Predictable quadratic-variation stabilization is not a condition defining \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) and is not proved from bounded schedules; it is an additional filtration-side antecedent for general CLT and coverage statements. Its verification for the Rademacher lower-bound supports is construction-specific. The Rademacher variance limits separate only when \(\rho>0\); at \(\rho=0\) their gap vanishes. The \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) CR2 fluctuation bound is only an upper bound, so \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) is a benchmark crossover rather than a proved exact noise-order elbow. Positive results remain restricted to the homogeneous fixed-size design.
body.honest_scope: The exact Kneser covariance, finite-sample design variance, schedule-uniform dense projection expansion, and CR2 variance and ratio expansions are unconditional design-based conclusions under their stated fixed-size design and boundedness conditions. The ambient class \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) additionally imposes scaled-variance nondegeneracy but does not impose predictable quadratic-variation stabilization. For every array in that class, the centered martingale CLT, CR2 studentized limits, Wald coverage, and sparse studentization conclusion are implications whose explicit additional antecedent is \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\); no claim is made that bounded schedules establish it. The sparse result drops \(N_n^2/n\to0\) but trades the comparator's Assumption 1 for that filtration-side premise. The exact software identity is tied to the stated equal-group unweighted intercept-plus-binary-treatment call and versioned package semantics. The impossibility theorem assumes \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\). It holds on additive no-interference schedules and therefore transfers upward to arbitrary bounded composition interference; its support arrays satisfy predictable-variation stability by the separate Rademacher calculation even though the ambient class does not require it. When \(\rho=0\), the projection correction and Rademacher limit gap vanish. No finite-sample CR2 conservativeness or variable-group-size extension is asserted.
